name: Pellaea

project_scope.note: Genus teaching framework only. None of the three source-pool species is currently in the canonical species manifest. Approved Taxa Installer owns admission and installation; do not imply these species have canonical learner cards.

look_here_first: Find the stipe (frond stalk) and rachis (main blade axis), then inspect how the pinnae attach and whether the rachis zigzags. On a fertile frond, flip the segments over: the rolled-under margins protect marginal sporangia (false indusia). Photograph both surfaces.
shared_traits: Ferns reproduce by spores, not flowers or seeds.
Divided fronds with marginal or submarginal sori, often sheltered by reflexed segment edges.
Dry rocky or cliff-crevice habitats can be normal for cliffbrakes; habitat alone does not identify species.

comparison_matrix.P. atropurpurea: dark purple to brown; short curled hairs can be present
comparison_matrix.P. ovata: often tan to brown and conspicuously zigzag between pinnae
comparison_matrix.P. wrightiana: often dark, comparatively straighter axis; confirm on multiple mature fronds

comparison_matrix.P. atropurpurea: pinnae often contrasted by shape and size along the frond; inspect basal pinnae
comparison_matrix.P. ovata: broadly triangular/ovate overall frond; pinnae frequently directed backward along zigzag axis
comparison_matrix.P. wrightiana: narrower fronds with relatively small segments; compare same-scale mature fertile fronds

comparison_matrix.P. atropurpurea: rachis hairs and segment attachment in macro
comparison_matrix.P. ovata: zigzag rachis and pinna direction together
comparison_matrix.P. wrightiana: narrow blade outline, segment dimensions and rachis character together

quick_key.if: Rachis conspicuously zigzag; pinnae often reflexed/backward pointing
quick_key.then: Pellaea ovata candidate — verify fertile frond and pinna details

quick_key.if: Rachis dark purple with short curly hairs; frond not strongly zigzag
quick_key.then: Pellaea atropurpurea candidate — inspect stipe/rachis macro

quick_key.if: Frond comparatively narrow, small segments, axis relatively straight
quick_key.then: Pellaea wrightiana candidate — confirm mature frond morphology; not a color-only ID

cautions: The matrix is a provisional teaching framework from source-pool/family reference material; exact species keys, variation, and measurements require Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review before being treated as final.
Stipe color changes with age and light; use mature fertile fronds, not a single young frond.
Sterile fronds and drought-stressed fronds may distort segment size and overall outline.
Marginal sori and rolled margins help recognize this fern group but are not sufficient to distinguish these three species.
No canonical species cards exist yet for this genus; do not link to fabricated species pages.

lookalikes.difference: Also xeric rock ferns with marginal sori and false indusia; compare scale/hair cover and segment shape under magnification, then verify accepted genus.
Often conspicuously scaly on the underside; examine pinna/pinnule scales before using habit alone.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Three matched entire mature fertile fronds on scale background, both surfaces
Stipe and rachis color/hair macro with scale, including curly hairs in P. atropurpurea
P. ovata zigzag rachis with arrows at pinna insertion and backward-facing pinnae
P. wrightiana segment dimensions and pinna attachments with scale
Rolled fertile segment margins opened enough to reveal sporangia without mislabeling false indusium
Dry-rock habitat plus basal stipe and rhizome when visible

handoffs.task: Verify accepted Pellaea concepts and exact key characters (rachis hairs, zigzag angle, pinna orientation, blade width, segment measurements) from regional flora before locking species comparisons.
Check approved Master Plant Pool rows and taxonomy decisions for three Pellaea taxa; install species only through installer lane.
Acquire exact-species licensed close-ups corresponding to diagnostic-photo checklist after taxonomy verification.
